note: The ii–V–I as open 7th shapes in the two keys where all three are open chords: the C shapes heard and strummed in time, then the G shapes, then both keys back to back on one strum-along. The open shapes are the lesson, so the keys stay written (no key moves) and the chords stay letters, counted the long way once per key; the tempo is moves (60 to 80). Every strum-along has its pattern. Folds in the separate C and G shape drills.

exercise.title: ii–V–I open 7th shapes in C and G
exercise.why: The ii–V–I is the same three-chord move in every key, so once its open shapes sit under your fingers in C, the shapes in G are the same move with new grips.

cells.text: Dm7 is the 2nd chord in the key of C, G7 is the 5th and Cmaj7 is the 1st: in that order they make the ii–V–I. Press a chord box below to hear it, then fret each shape and pick the strings one at a time to check they ring.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down on every beat, one bar for each chord.
If a change comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.
In the key of G the ii–V–I is Am7, D7 and Gmaj7. Press a chord box below to hear it, then fret each shape and check it rings.

Press Play below to start the metronome again. The boxes run through the ii–V–I in C, then in G: strum down on every beat and change keys without stopping.
Practice until the six shapes are in your muscle memory: your fingers find each grip before its beat 1.
